transcript.author: murray-bookchin

Every ecological problem is at root a social one: the domination of nature follows from hierarchy and competition. The remedy is directly democratic municipalities deciding what to produce and why.

transcript.author: kohei-saito
transcript.text: I oppose the claim. Capital has to expand value without limit, and that drive keeps widening the metabolic rift between society and nature. Efficiency gains get reinvested into more throughput. Absolute decoupling at the speed required has not happened. Abundance has to come from the commons and from free time, not from more production. That is the case for degrowth communism.

transcript.author: pierre-charbonnier
transcript.text: I doubt the claim. Modern freedoms grew out of abundant land, colonies and coal, so the hope of decoupling keeps the old bargain where liberty depends on plenty. transcript.author: giorgos-kallis
transcript.text: I oppose the claim. transcript.author: eduardo-gudynas

transcript.author: yayo-herrero

interviews.reaction: Decoupling is a technical promise that announces its benefits and stays silent about the problems it will create. Efficiency feeds a technological system that grows by its own logic, and no one steers it toward a limit.

interviews.author: yayo-herrero
interviews.reaction: Decoupling is not credible because growth accounting leaves out its own foundations: the ecosystems it draws down and the unpaid care work, mostly done by women, that keeps people alive. The task is to put sustaining life at the centre of the economy.

interviews.author: murray-bookchin
interviews.reaction: A grow-or-die market economy cannot respect limits for long, so decoupling fails as a technical fix. The ecological crisis comes from hierarchy and competition. Only directly democratic municipalities that decide what to produce and why can bring the economy back into balance with nature.

interviews.author: arne-naess
interviews.reaction: Decoupling is shallow ecology. It asks how to pollute less per unit of output and never asks why rich societies need ever more output. Staying within limits takes a life rich in ends and simple in means, and room for other beings to unfold.

interviews.author: edward-o-wilson
interviews.reaction: Growth is not the enemy in itself. Decoupling counts only if it stops habitat loss, the main driver of extinction. Carbon cuts and land sparing are not enough on their own. Half of the land and sea must be formally set aside for the rest of life.

interviews.author: timothy-morton
interviews.reaction: Decoupling pictures the economy here and Nature over there, as if they could be pulled apart. Global warming is a hyperobject that everything already sits inside, economies included. Nothing exists outside it to decouple into, so the claim depends on a picture ecological thought has to give up.

interviews.author: john-bellamy-foster
interviews.reaction: Decoupling mistakes a social rupture for a technical ratio. Capital accumulation widens the metabolic rift between society and the earth, and efficiency gains under a growth imperative expand throughput. Staying within planetary boundaries requires transforming social relations of production.

interviews.author: james-lovelock
interviews.reaction: Decoupling comes too late. Earth is one self-regulating system with nonlinear feedbacks, and the total load on it keeps rising. It may jump to a hotter state whatever national accounts show. The task is a planned retreat powered by nuclear energy, not more growth.

interviews.author: robyn-eckersley
interviews.reaction: Decoupling fast enough is doubtful, and markets will not deliver it on their own. Ecological limits can only be set and enforced by a transformed state, one answerable to everyone its decisions affect, including people not yet born and other species.

interviews.author: andre-gorz
interviews.reaction: Decoupling, even if possible, leaves untouched who decides what is produced and why. Growth serves capital's valorisation and is steered by experts. The answer is sufficiency, a common norm of enough set by those concerned, together with tools people can understand and control.

interviews.author: pierre-charbonnier
interviews.reaction: Decoupling is doubtful because it keeps the modern bargain that tied freedom to abundant land, colonies and fossil energy. Clean energy put in place of coal leaves that dependence unexamined. The decisive task is political: finding a freedom that does not rest on material expansion.

interviews.author: maria-mies
interviews.reaction: Opposed. Growth rests on unpaid work by women, peasants and colonies, which it treats as free like air and water. What looks like decoupling in Northern statistics moves the damage onto them. The alternative is an economy built around producing life.

interviews.author: maristella-svampa
interviews.reaction: Decoupling measured in importing economies hides displaced extraction. Under the commodities consensus, governments of left and right expanded mining, soy and oil exports, so Northern efficiency depends on Southern frontiers. Growth stays coupled to territories, not decoupled from damage.
